reasons: Minnie claims entry at 6:44 by the service clock, after the independently logged 6:38 lock. Her clock cannot be explained by the fast gallery clock.

Her claimed task is adjusting an internal lamp. The dated installation photo has an external standing light and an open cradle, with no enclosed overhead lamp. Her account matches the superseded proposal rather than an actual visit.
She explicitly mentions business around Grant's salon, where the empty coupe stayed during the poisoning opportunity. Her lighting grievance supplies motive.

Many others tell impossible late-entry stories but know the real open apparatus. Others invent features from the obsolete proposal but claim an early visit rather than a late alibi. Minnie is the only person in both categories.
uncertainty: This is the strongest accusation rather than strict proof: an innocent guest could theoretically invent a late visit using old plans too, while the admitted salon business is not itself poisoning evidence. The published case creates a unique double contradiction, so the intended answer becomes clear.
experience: I liked finding that both the programme and the display proposal were stale. The installation photograph gives an enjoyable visual comparison rather than a flat written verdict. Several innocent liars made my early suspicion genuinely tentative. Once all testimony and both late reports are visible together, however, the puzzle becomes a simple intersection of two false-account types.
confusion: The excerpt provides no in-character reason for me to accuse aloud versus write a private ballot; a real facilitator needs an explicit transition.

The repeated other-business sentence seems like an unresolved placeholder. In a live room I would ask those people what their business actually was, and I am unsure which details they may invent before Coming Clean.
Minnie insists the security controller is separate from her lighting console; that clears a potential sabotage theory but also directs attention straight back to her impossible personal account.
repetitive_dialogue: Eight late-entry guests use the same other-business sentence.
The early obsolete-cabinet group repeats the same outside-enclosure ending.
Almost all motives are donor blackmail or withheld payment. Funny voice helps, but the basic grievance rhythm repeats.
accidental_giveaway: No confession is accidentally spoken. Minnie nevertheless stands out stylistically because her opportunity speech ends with a salon admission where the other late-visit speeches have an identical secrecy disclaimer.
concrete_improvements: Replace generic repeated secrecy endings with character-specific concealment: what exact secret they are protecting and a distinct way of deflecting, without premature exoneration.
Let multiple innocent guests explicitly admit salon visits during the relevant interval so Minnie's salon sentence is not a authored-role flag.
Make every guilty/innocent opportunity box stylistically comparable within its character. The culprit should stand out through evidence, not through a sentence pattern exception.

Consider one or two innocent guests who also have a double-inaccurate alibi, with a separate discoverable reason or independent evidence resolving their involvement. Simply adding liars in disjoint categories still produces an obvious two-column classifier.

Have the host repeat the installation-photo date and allow a closer look at the photograph; the open forks versus obsolete glass are visually useful, but older guests may need more than a small clue-card image.
limitations: Independent scripted transcript assessment by an AI, not an interactive human party. Perfect access to the entire transcript makes contradiction comparison easier than listening across a table.
protocol: Read only own three stages and the three named shared images. Saved stage1 before stage2 and stage2 before stage3; no Coming Clean or organizer/source files opened.
